description: A soft, silvery-white radioactive metal with symbol Ac and atomic number 89. It was discovered by André-Louis Debierne in 1899, and the actinide series of 15 elements is named after actinium.
uses: Its current applications include use as a neutron source and an agent for radiation therapy. It has no significant industrial use due to its scarcity, high price, and radioactivity.
characteristics: Actinium reacts rapidly with oxygen and moisture in air, forming a white coating of actinium oxide that prevents further oxidation. It assumes oxidation state +3 in nearly all its chemical compounds and glows in the dark with a pale blue light due to its strong radioactivity. The naturally occurring isotope 227Ac decays with a half-life of 21.772 years, predominantly emitting beta particles and sometimes alpha particles.
